> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **31** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4e5e79b20d36392a75344f7dc003583a35077af7` — the merge of head `79aa35b1c41bba90effa9e6abbf567c8a9da4bac` into base `09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4e5e79b20d36392a75344f7dc003583a35077af7 && git checkout 4e5e79b20d36392a75344f7dc003583a35077af7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88 79aa35b1c41bba90effa9e6abbf567c8a9da4bac && git checkout -B drift-repro 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88 && git merge --no-ff 79aa35b1c41bba90effa9e6abbf567c8a9da4bac

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 09e07c259a633eb02fdb29bedfe911e808529f88` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `569f28a5c218928e82c8c12e2f724de46b948399`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/core/src/lite-kernel.ts, packages/core/src/cloud-managed.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts, .changeset/25294-is-cloud-managed.md + packages/core/src/utils/env.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/core/package.json, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/types/src/env.ts, docker/Dockerfile

Adversarial read of head `569f28a5c` against merge base `fb7501bc6` (net diff +277/−1, 6 files), card #25294 (claim 6351990387, amendment 6352016263, dev report 6352917588), ruling 6341690661 on #25083 (Q2 → D), hand-off 6349658918 on #20966, ruling 6352436010 on #25292, declaration 6352046857 on #6024, and the head's check-runs. Tier: the file list decides no schema or rules face and the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` alone would owe the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the seat raised it to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` in the claim (a boot refusal on the auth path), and that tier is served here.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. The ruling, sentence by sentence (Q2 → D).**
- *One accessor, beside `isHostKernelComposition`, in `core/src/stack-auth.ts`, synchronous boolean.* Held: `isCloudManaged(): boolean` at `stack-auth.ts:172`, no arguments, no promise, reachable from `@objectstack/core` through `index.ts:39` `export * from './stack-auth.js'` and the package's `exports["."]` map. Named exactly as the ruling spells it (no `_ENABLED`, not `isManaged()`).
- *The ONE reader of `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED`.* Held: `git grep OS_CLOUD_MANAGED` on the head tree outside changelogs hits the changeset, the new test, two comments, and one `getEnv` call — `decideCloudManaged()` at `stack-auth.ts:188`. Readers on the base: 0 (the PR body's reading, re-measured). `isCloudManaged()` is called from exactly two production sites, `kernel.ts:535` and `lite-kernel.ts:94`.
- *Pin 9, four cases.* Each pinned in `cloud-managed.test.ts` and each traced through the code: (a) `NODE_ENV=development` + variable → `production` is false → `managed: true`; (b) production + variable + `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` non-blank → `managed: true`; (c) production + variable + key unset/blank → `refusal` thrown, message opens with the variable and names the missing binding and both remedies; (d) no variable → `getEnv` returns `undefined` → `managed: false` on every boot, key or no key.
- *"Production" = not `--dev`, not `NODE_ENV=test`.* `isDevelopmentBoot(undefined)` reads only `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'`; the accessor then excludes `NODE_ENV === 'test'` explicitly. Unset `NODE_ENV` is production, which matches `serve.ts:2178` (defaults it to `production`) and `docker/Dockerfile:107` (`ENV NODE_ENV=production`), so a self-hosted image carrying a copied env file is refused — the case the ruling exists for. `--dev` reaches the accessor only through `NODE_ENV`: `serve.ts:2176` sets `development` **only when `NODE_ENV` is unset** (#11113: an explicit `NODE_ENV` wins for the whole gate family). So `NODE_ENV=production os serve --dev` gives serve `isDev = true` while the accessor reads production, and with the variable and no key it refuses. That is the one divergence between serve's `isDev` and the accessor; it is loud, names the remedy, and agrees with every other `NODE_ENV`-gated behaviour in that process. Not a failure of the ruling; see ③ for the prose it affects.
- *A hosted container, both misreads traced.* Misread as non-production (a container with `NODE_ENV` development or test): the accessor answers `true` with the fuse dormant — the runtime is hosted, so managed mode is on and nothing is lost. Misread as production with no key: refuses every hosted container — which happens only if the cloud binds the key by plugin option alone. The in-repo evidence says it does not: `cloud-connection-plugin.ts:78` and `connection-credential-store.ts:8` document `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` as "injected by the cloud into the runtimes it hosts", and the ruling itself names `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` first as the binding. The cloud repository was not read by the dev (stated) nor by this review (outside the inputs) — see the observation under ③.
- *Not in `serve.ts`.* Held: `serve.ts` is untouched; the fuse lives in `stack-auth.ts` and is read by both kernels. Every `bootstrap()` in `packages/core/src` is covered (`kernel.ts:526`, `lite-kernel.ts:88`; `ObjectKernelBase` declares none and no other package defines a kernel class), which is what "every kernel in the process reads the same fact" asks for, the cloud's per-environment kernels included.

**2. One source for "control plane bound".** `resolveControlPlaneApiKey(configured?)` = `(configured ?? getEnv('OS_CLOUD_API_KEY') ?? '').trim()`. Against the replaced inline `(this.cfg.controlPlaneApiKey ?? process.env.OS_CLOUD_API_KEY ?? '').trim()` it is behaviour-identical for every input: config set (wins, trimmed), env set (trimmed), both (config wins), config `''` (wins as `''` in both — `??` passes an empty string through), env `''` (`getEnv`'s `||` returns `undefined`, `??` yields `''`; the inline form yielded `''` too), whitespace (trimmed to `''` either way). `platformManaged = cloudApiKey !== ''` at `:336` is unchanged, so cloud-connection's answer is byte-identical and the fuse's `resolveControlPlaneApiKey() === ''` is the same predicate without the option arm. The other `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` reader, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1244`, selects a bearer for a catalog fetch (env key, else the bound `oscc_` token) — a credential use, not a second derivation of the "bound" fact; the CLI publish commands read it as a flag default. No inline copy of the fact remains. The accepted cost (a production boot binding the key by plugin option alone, with the variable set, is refused) is stated in the PR body ("The known cost") and in the changeset ("One caveat"), and is the shape the seat ruled in amendment 6352016263.

**3. Where the fuse fires.** First read of the accessor; `ObjectKernel.bootstrap()` after the "already bootstrapped" guard and before `state = 'initializing'`; `LiteKernel.bootstrap()` after `validateState('idle')` at the same point — both before any plugin's `init()`, which the boot test pins by an empty `calls` array on rejection. Memoization: `cloudManagedVerdict` holds either `{ managed }` or `{ refusal }`; `isCloudManaged()` rethrows the stored refusal on every later read, so no read answers `true` after a refusal without `resetCloudManagedForTesting()` (pinned, including the case where the key appears after the refusal). First read before the environment is final: nothing calls the accessor at module load — the two call sites are inside `bootstrap()`; a test that imports then sets the environment must reset, which the PR body prescribes. `resetCloudManagedForTesting()`: exported, named in the PR body and the changeset as the hand-off asked, JSDoc says "never called by a boot". It is unguarded; weighed: a caller able to invoke it already controls `process.env` and could pre-empt the fuse before the first read, so a guard defends nothing, and a `NODE_ENV=test`-only guard would break the PR's own memo test (its second reset runs under `production`). Acceptable as a plain test helper. A boot WITHOUT the variable: `getEnv` returns `undefined`, `{ managed: false }` is stored, no throw, no log line, one env read and one module-binding write — observable behaviour byte-identical to the base. The LiteKernel site is a dev deviation from the claim's "`ObjectKernel.bootstrap()`"; accepted, the ruling's "every kernel in the process" requires it.

**4. The dev's open question — verdict: A stands; no code change.** The ruling spells the switch as `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED=1`; both readings satisfy it, so the choice is by direction. Treating `true`/`0`/`yes` as off is a lenient alias in a consumer on an internal contract (Prime Directive 12) and fails CLOSED silently — a hosted runtime with a mistyped switch would run with every managed-mode door open and nothing would say so. The repo's recorded `OS_ALLOW_*` vocabulary (`types/env.ts:563`) names exactly that flaw of a strict `=== '1'` — "fails CLOSED … reads to an operator as the flag being broken" — and cured it there by widening the truthy set; this PR cures it by refusing loudly with the value and the remedy named, which is the right cure for a switch whose only producer (the cloud, cloud#3133) writes the literal `1` and whose off state is "remove it". `0`/`false` are refused too; the message says to remove the variable, and no in-repo producer writes them. Loud and safe; the ruling is not narrowed.

**5. Public surface.** Three new exports of `@objectstack/core` (`isCloudManaged`, `resolveControlPlaneApiKey`, `resetCloudManagedForTesting`), all reachable from `exports["."]`. No existing export changed or removed. Core's public surface is ledgered by no gate (`api-surface/` exists for `packages/spec` only), so nothing to regenerate. The new test is reached by `packages/core/tsconfig.test.json` (`src/**/*`, tests not excluded) and by vitest's `local` project.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25294-is-cloud-managed.md`: `@objectstack/core` **patch**, `@objectstack/cloud-connection` **patch**; both packages publish (`private` absent) and both are listed. Body carries line-initial `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines, identically. Judged right: three added exports widen the accepted set (`yes (widening)`, a well-formed member of the closed pair); no authorable metadata key, value or meaning moves (`none` → `patch` by the Post-Task rule "none takes patch"); not breaking (no export removed, no ADR-0087 disposition owed). The changeset names the behaviour change a self-hosted deployment can hit (a copied env file now refuses) and the option-only caveat, which is what an upgrading reader greps for. `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviations (5), all accepted:** attribution link to the card thread; session-URL footer on the PR body (AGENTS.md's form); the LiteKernel site (required by the ruling, see ①.3); two lines in cloud-connection instead of one (the import); the MCP reviewer request skipped (writes forbidden) — none changes the verdict.
- **Open question (1):** answered in ①.4 — A, as built; not a FAIL item.
- **Cross-lane:** declaration 6352046857 on #6024 names the `cloud-connection-plugin.ts` line, states "not a claim on any `domain:cli` card", and matches the diff (`:144` import, `:317` derivation). Amendment 6352016263 widened the claim's file surface to it first. `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`: success.
- **Downstream consumers:** ruling 6352436010 on #25292 consumes `isCloudManaged()` (one served line in `getPublicConfig()`) and `resetCloudManagedForTesting()` from this head; the hand-off's calling shape (`import { isCloudManaged } from '@objectstack/core'`, synchronous, per request and at AuthManager construction, tests under `NODE_ENV=test` with a reset) is met: under `test` the fuse is off and the variable alone reads managed, pinned.
- **Card relation:** `Fixes #25294` (the engine card is fully delivered) and `Part of #25083` (zero verb beside it); `Part-of PR must not also close its card`: success; `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`: success.
- **Check-runs on the head at posting:** see the tally line below; no failure on any run; no red to attribute.
- **Observations for the seat (none a FAIL item):**
  1. The one fact this PR's safety on hosted containers rests on is that the cloud injects `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` as an environment variable on every runtime it hosts (not only as the `controlPlaneApiKey` option). In-repo text and the ruling both say so; the cloud side was not read in this lane. Ruling 6341690661 names the consequence of getting it wrong ("would take every hosted container down at the next pin move"), so confirm `ObjectOSContainer.envVars` carries the key before the next pin move lands this.
  2. Prose for the seat's ACCEPT (the changeset and PR-body faces are the dispatch seat's): "`--dev`, which sets `NODE_ENV=development`" is exact only when `NODE_ENV` is unset (`serve.ts:2176`); with an explicit `NODE_ENV=production` beside `--dev` the accessor reads production. One qualifying clause would make the CHANGELOG sentence match the code.
  3. The fuse reads `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` at `bootstrap()` entry; cloud-connection reads it at `kernel:ready`. Both are after "config load", so a host that sets the variable between config load and kernel boot (the plugin's documented window) satisfies both; only a mutation from inside a plugin's `init()` could make the two disagree, and nothing in the tree does that.
  4. `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1244` still spells the env arm of the credential inline (pre-existing, a credential selection rather than the "bound" fact); if the seat wants one spelling for the env read too, that is a separate housekeeping line in the `domain:cli` lane, not this PR's.

Check-runs on `569f28a5c` at posting (2026-10-22T22:53Z): 39 runs — 25 success, 7 skipped, 7 in progress, 0 failed. Still running: Test Core (1/6), Test Core (2/6), Test Core (3/6), Test Core (4/6), Test Core (5/6), Test Core (6/6), Type Check · workspace — the seat re-reads these before queueing; a red on them is this PR's to attribute. Required contexts complete and green: Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-dhsqgf`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FaVyM6YvQLg9CsjPVCYc5K`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · `domain:engine` seat 2 (seat post #20966) · `os-bill` · `session_01FaVyM6YvQLg9CsjPVCYc5K` · 2026-10-22T22:57Z · head `79aa35b1c41bba90effa9e6abbf567c8a9da4bac` · card #25294 (p1, `Part of #25083`).

1. **Form:** draft, `Fixes #25294`, `Part of #25083`, assignee `os-bill`, 6 files. `check-governed-merges --pr 25306`: not governed, under 3000 changed lines ⇒ ordinary queue landing.
2. **Premise measured:** the dev report 6352917588: 0 readers of `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED` on the base; cloud-connection's inline derivation moved to core as `resolveControlPlaneApiKey(configured?)`, behaviour-identical; the fuse ablation turns 5 pins red and leaves the 3 run-cases green, and each kernel's call ablated alone turns its own pin red.
3. **Gates:** contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` **PASS** 6353098458 on `569f28a5c`. The head then moved to this head by one prose commit (the changeset's `--dev` sentence gains the review's qualifier: `--dev` sets `NODE_ENV=development` only when it is unset), and the seat made the same correction in the PR body; no code or test byte moved, so the record governs this head. Landing waits for every check on this head to read completed green.
4. **Accepted deviations:**
   - The fuse also fires in `LiteKernel.bootstrap()`, as the ruling's "every kernel in the process" requires.
   - The file surface widened by cloud-connection's derivation line (claim amendment 6352016263); cross-lane declaration 6352046857 on #6024, not a claim.
   - A non-empty value other than `1` is refused loudly (the review's verdict: a lenient alias would fail closed silently on a mistyped switch).
   - `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (three new public exports of `@objectstack/core`), `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` for core and cloud-connection.
5. **Out of scope, disposed:**
   - The fuse reads the environment only: a hosted runtime binding the control plane by the plugin option alone would be refused. The in-repo record says the cloud injects `OS_CLOUD_API_KEY` as an environment variable; the seat has asked the maintainer to confirm on the cloud side before the next pin move.
   - `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts:1244` still spells the environment arm inline for a credential fetch (pre-existing, `domain:cli`); not filed.
6. **Landing:** once every check on this head is green, the seat flips ready and arms auto-merge through the relay; the card closes on merge by `Fixes #25294`, and #25083's services half and #25292's joint PR are unblocked.
